items.detail: S1 HI (THINGS VLA) and S2 (WSRT) observe the same 21-cm HI over 0.3-15.1 kpc; S5 Begeman (not in bundle) overlaps both. Counting the same HI once requires a declared rule; none is made.
S1 stars (Leroy, M/L applied) vs SPARC .sfb/.dens (not in bundle): fixed conversion ratio 1.2568 between conventions; inclination 72 vs 73; no source chosen.
S1 stars end at 15.1 kpc; no observed stellar profile covers 21.42-44.08 kpc (12 queries); SPARC .dens rows there are inferred extrapolation; the last query lies beyond the last .dens row.
S1 H2 MISSING rows are null, never zero (row indices computed below); no other H2 source found in the searched paths.

SPARC catalogue geometry extraction V001 QUARANTINED; V002 inert pending schema provenance (0344/0345-B). S1 and S2 both use the Leroy table4 working plane (i 72, PA 215) and D 13.8 Mpc without uncertainty; these values are SECONDARY (correction C4/C6); the S2 plane is not a warp solution.
No map from these observational records to native UNT record-surface inputs exists (S1 table_level raw_to_native_map, checked null). Owned by native-physics work, not by this adapter.
S2 has no measurement uncertainty (unknown, not zero); its mask uses a kinematic window (reduction dependency); 40.14-48.17 kpc annulus is review-flagged (43.66% zero/replaced).

S1 per-ring rms fields: whether each is a measurement uncertainty or a descriptive azimuthal scatter is not established locally; e=1 on HI/stars carries ReadMe Note 3 "upper limit" (quarantined); e=0 is literal with unresolved meaning; no replacement errors.
Queries are emitted separately. No mapping, interpolation or extrapolation from source grids to query radii is performed.

Only "Including helium" (Leroy ReadMe Note 2) is primary-stated. SECONDARY: helium 1.36, X_CO, CO line ratio, stellar M/L relation (C1-C3), S1/S2 geometry values i/PA/D (C4, C6), S2 centre citation (C6). PROGRAM-DECLARED: 1.25e20 per Msun/pc^2 and the S2 helium factor and working plane (C5, C6). Carry rules unchanged; primary verification pending.
